heroHeadline: Merz Battles CDU Leadership Crisis as Germany's May Inflation Eases to 2.6% and Elderly Care Reform Erupts
heroSubtitle: Chancellor Merz faced rare internal CDU succession discussions (May 26–28), triggered by a Bild report citing his record-low 16% approval rating; he delivered an economic revival speech declaring 'Germany has the strength for a new beginning.' Germany's May 2026 CPI fell to 2.6% (Destatis flash, May 29) from April's 2.9%, though energy prices remained elevated at +6.6% YoY amid Middle East tensions. The EU Commission's Spring 2026 forecast cut Germany's full-year GDP growth estimate to 0.6% due to the energy price shock. The CDU/CSU Bundestag group on May 30 proposed requiring elderly Germans to exhaust home equity before receiving state nursing care — igniting a sharp coalition dispute with SPD partners over Germany's €22B+ care insurance deficit.
